title: add vpc control plane provisioning terraform: subnets, endpoints, sgs, peering, route53
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Add first-class Terraform module and environment examples to provision the VPC control plane resources required for Redwood Private deployments on AWS. Motivation: customers installing Private control planes often need a repeatable, secure VPC topology with well-configured subnets, service endpoints, security groups, VPC peering to customer VPCs, and Route53 delegation for internal DNS. This module codifies best-practices (AZ-aware subnets, endpoint-only NAT minimization, least-privilege SGs) and provides example environment overlays and a dry-run test harness.

What this PR does: - Introduce terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane with main.tf/variables.tf/outputs.tf and documented examples (examples/aws). - Create templates for Route53 delegation and cross-account peering acceptance (templates/route53.tf, examples/aws/peering.tf). - Add managed VPC endpoints for S3, ECR, KMS, STS, EC2/ECR (where applicable) with configurability to opt-in/opt-out per environment. - Implement security groups scoped to control plane CIDR and minimal ports for control-plane <-> runtime communication, and a separate SG for management plane (bastion/SSH/metrics). - Provide outputs for peering connection IDs, delegated hosted zone IDs, and endpoint ARNs for downstream automation. - Add example environment config that wires the module with a remote S3 state backend and DynamoDB lock table and documents upgrade and rollback steps.

Upgrade/rollback notes: The module intentionally avoids destructive changes in default flows: subnet CIDR and AZ assignments are input-driven (no in-module replacements). Peering and Route53 delegation create clear resource dependencies and outputs to make rollbacks possible by first removing dependent consumers (see README). State locking with S3/DynamoDB is required in env examples to prevent drift during multi-operator upgrades.

Testing performed: - terraform validate and tflint run in CI. - Integration plan/apply executed in a staging account with minimal example (staging environment) to verify endpoint provisioning, SG connectivity, and route53 delegation propagation. - Peering acceptance automation tested via example cross-account IAM role. Known limitations: AWS-managed route propagation for peering across complex route tables requires manual verification in some customer networks; documented in README.

Why this lives in redwood-terraform: centralizes the VPC control plane provisioning used by Private installer and the private-control-plane Helm chart; examples will be consumed by redwood-private-installer and redwood-helm-charts during customer onboarding.

review_conversation: Ethan Wagner: Please ensure that endpoints are opt-in by default for regions where they are chargeable. Also, add an output for endpoint ARNs so downstream automation can wire them.
Asha Patel: Good catch — endpoints are now opt-in via variable 'enable_service_endpoints' (default=false) and outputs include endpoint_arns.
Lina Gomez: Security group looks broad on the management SG (port 22 open to 0.0.0.0/0). Can we restrict to documented bastion CIDRs?
Asha Patel: Updated management SG to reference 'management_allowed_cidrs' variable and set example to a narrow CIDR in staging. Added note in README about jumpbox patterns.
Marcus Li: CI showed intermittent 'apply' failure on peering acceptance due to eventual consistency. Recommend adding a short retry loop in examples or an explicit wait resource.
Asha Patel: Added depends_on and a null_resource with local-exec retry for peering acceptance in the example. Also documented in the upgrade notes.
Ethan Wagner: Approving with minor doc nits (link to private-installer usage).
Lina Gomez: Approved after SG tightening.
release_notes: Added terraform module 'vpc-control-plane' to provision control-plane VPC resources for Redwood Private on AWS. Features: AZ-aware subnets, configurable service endpoints, scoped security groups, VPC peering helpers, Route53 delegation templates, outputs for automation. See module README for upgrade/rollback steps and staging example.
